market.summary: A weaker open is likely. Wall Street fell again on Tuesday and GIFT Nifty points about 0.4% lower, with most of Asia down. Reports of US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island add risk for crude, though Brent is steady near $92.7. Foreign buying in India remains the main support.

points.text: GIFT Nifty at 25,259 at 7:21 IST, down 0.36%, pointing to a Nifty open about 128 points under Tuesday's 25,387 close.
US close on 17 Nov: Dow -1.64% to 50,759, S&P 500 -1.03% to 7,340.5, Nasdaq 100 -0.72%. Nvidia reported its quarter after the US close.
Asia this morning: Nikkei -0.5%, Hang Seng -0.6%, Shanghai -0.2%, KOSPI +0.8%. Brent is at $92.67 a barrel (-0.4%).
Reports late on 17 Nov of US strikes on Qeshm Island, Iran; the US military had released no official details.
FIIs bought about ₹4,195 Cr in cash on 17 Nov (provisional). They have been net buyers of about ₹84,167 Cr this month up to 16 Nov, while DIIs sold on every session.
Foreign investors have put a record $9.53 billion into Indian shares so far in November.

market.watch: Whether the gap-down open is bought by FIIs, plus crude after the Iran reports. Your trades' exit rules are on closing prices, so an opening dip alone is not an exit.

GROWW.summary: No new news since last evening. Early investor Ribbit Capital sold 8.7 crore shares (1.4% of the company) in a ₹1,905 Cr block at ₹219, 2.6% under Monday's close. BlackRock, Fidelity, Kotak MF, NPS Trust, Norges Bank and others took it all, and the stock still closed higher at ₹227.53. A large supply overhang was absorbed by long-term funds without damaging the price, which supports the drift. You are +2.2R with the stop at cost.

points.text: Ribbit Capital entities sold 8.7 crore shares at ₹219 (₹1,905.3 Cr) in a block deal on 17 Nov.
The block was 1.4% of Groww's equity, priced 2.63% below Monday's close of ₹224.92.

NSE block-deal data lists buyers at ₹219, including Kotak Mahindra MF (about 2.05 crore shares across four trades), BlackRock funds (about 1.26 crore), Fidelity funds (about 0.78 crore), HDFC Life (26 lakh), NPS Trust (23 lakh) and Norges Bank (11.5 lakh).
US broker Robinhood fell 7.5% on Monday, but Groww closed up 1.2% at ₹227.53 on 1.7x volume.

GROWW.watch: A weak open may test ₹219 (block price, about the 10 EMA 219.01); the plan sells half only on a close below it. Stop is at cost (₹200.80).

SEJALLTD.summary: No new filing since last evening. The stock bounced 6.9% to ₹927.85, back above your cost (₹884.13) and the 10 EMA (₹890). This comes after Monday's close of ₹867.60 was below both, and the plan had said to exit the rest then. The Magnumtuff glass-business purchase (₹40.80 Cr) agreement was signed on 14 Nov. The 16 Nov filing about a promoter-group member's death could not be opened, so its effect is not verified. The monthly RSI still shows a bearish divergence.

points.text: Business Transfer Agreement signed on 14 Nov to buy Magnumtuff India's architectural and automotive glass business, proposed at ₹40.80 Cr.
16 Nov intimation of the death of a promoter-group member (PDF not readable from this check).

SEJALLTD.watch: A close below ₹890 (10 EMA) sells half, below ₹884 (cost) exits the rest; a close above ₹930 is +1R.

INDHOTEL.summary: No new news since last evening. Indian Hotels made a new closing high at ₹901.55, about +2.6R, with strong hands and accumulation. Stable crude (Brent near $92) keeps travel costs steady.

points.text: Brent Jan-27 futures at about $92.8 on 17 Nov; Kotak Neo reports Hormuz shipments have nearly returned to pre-war levels.

INDHOTEL.watch: Plan sells half on a close below the 10 EMA (₹876) and the rest below the 20 EMA (₹846); last close ₹901.55. Watch crude after the Iran reports.

Nifty Media was among the sectors up 0.5-0.9% on 17 Nov.
